finding: A counted reconciliation exists and is real rather than asserted: coverage.py routes two producing components that name no adapter, signer or store through one produce_artifact() boundary, refuses to register any digest no attestation resolves for, counts artifacts recorded against attestations resolvable in the same window, and a deliberate bypass write is caught (artifacts_produced 3, attestations_valid 2, unattested [bypass-artifact], reconciled false) with a second admission check refusing it. But the scope is the file itself: the two producers are defined in the same script, the manifest 'starts from an empty manifest' each run so the period is one process, the script is named in no gate (test.sh and provenance.json mention it zero times), and the platform's own producing paths carry no emission at all -- the reference runner mentions attest 0 times and the four-door composition harness that binds the capabilities mentions attest or provenance 0 times in its platform module. That is the misaligned anchor's 'some producing paths leave no record' plus 'nothing enumerates what was produced' for everything outside the demo, held up by an aligned-shaped mechanism that runs on nothing real, so it scores as existing rather than aligned.
gap: The mechanism is demonstrated, not installed. Missing: (a) produce_artifact() as the actual write path of the platform's runners rather than a local function with two in-file callers, so a component added later inherits emission by passing the boundary; (b) an enumeration of artifacts produced over a real period -- the runners' out/ trees, the ledgers, the evidence records -- against attestations emitted, instead of a manifest truncated at the start of each demo run; (c) the reconciliation and its bypass breakage wired into a gate that fails, since coverage.py is currently reachable only by running it by hand and no test would notice if it stopped working; (d) a structural refusal of the escape path -- inject_bypass appends straight to the manifest, so the escape is detected after the fact by counting rather than being refused or impossible, which is the weaker half of the aligned anchor.
